appraisal_events.evidence: dans son assurance et sa grandeur de déesse... fit à ces demi-dieux du Jockey-Club — qui à ce moment-là, et particulièrement M. de Palancy, furent les hommes que j'aurais le plus aimé être — un bonjour familier de vieille amie... on les vit, se retournant l'une vers l'autre, s'admirer réciproquement... 'La duchesse est un des êtres les plus nobles de Paris, de l'élite la plus raffinée, la plus choisie.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchesse's commanding late entrance, her practiced, familiar greeting of the most envied men in the room, her mutual admiration with her cousin the princesse, and Swann's remembered praise together present her, and by association her cousin and the men she favors, as supremely and effortlessly eminent.

appraisal_events.evidence: un effort à la fois patient et coûteux pour imiter les toilettes et le chic de la duchesse de Guermantes, faire seulement ressembler Mme de Cambremer à quelque pensionnaire provinciale, montée sur fil de fer, droite, sèche et pointue, un plumet de corbillard verticalement dressé dans les cheveux... Être reçue chez ces deux grandes dames était pourtant le but qu'elle poursuivait depuis dix ans... elle ne pouvait avoir l'air de quêter un salut... elle craignait de ne pouvoir vivre jusque-là.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's comparison reduces Mme de Cambremer's costly imitation of the duchesse's chic to a stiff, funereal caricature, while the surrounding narration shows her occupying a borrowed box, unable even to seek a greeting, after a decade of unsuccessful effort to be received by the two cousins.

status_effects.explanation: Her entrance and greetings are witnessed as an effortless display of supreme social command and old, familiar intimacy with the most desirable men present.
The mutual admiration between the cousins and the framing of both as inimitable originals mark the princesse's standing as well, though the entrance itself centers on the duchesse.
He is singled out by name as one of the men the duchesse greets with old familiarity, and whom the narrator most envies.
The narrator's simile reduces her appearance to a stiff, provincial, funereal caricature by contrast with the genuine article she imitates.
Despite a decade of patient pursuit, she remains outside the two grandes dames' circle, watching from a borrowed box without standing even to seek their acknowledgment.
